answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards and voting weight capped by that stake. A verified useful task earns fees; proven fraud or duplicate submissions slash the bond through a public challenge process. Splitting one agent into many identities does not create more stake or influence, so a sybil attacker must tie up proportionally more capital and risk losing it. A saffron delivery may be checked against a walnut receipt whose kernel hash anchors the evidence.
